claims.claim: Zalcitabine, a cytidine nucleoside analog, showed 80% absolute oral bioavailability in fasted patients, demonstrating that cytosine-based nucleosides can exceed the F>=20% threshold.
Lamivudine, another cytidine analog, showed absolute oral bioavailability of 69-87% across fasted patients and formulations, supporting high oral bioavailability for this class.
Mericitabine, a cytidine nucleoside prodrug, was reported to have excellent oral bioavailability in humans, though it is rapidly converted to its active metabolite.
Doxifluridine, a pyrimidine nucleoside, showed ~50-80% oral bioavailability in patients, further supporting that polar nucleosides can achieve F>=20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule (decitabine-like 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine) is present in the supplied records.
No information on cytidine deaminase-mediated first-pass metabolism or metabolic stability of the query is available in the cards or prior.
Transfer from modified cytidine analogs (e.g., zalcitabine, lamivudine) may not fully capture the query's deamination risk.
The physicochemical prior indicates unfavorable passive permeability, but active transport and the modest F threshold could compensate.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F>=20%) because all transferable L1 records for structurally related cytidine/pyrimidine nucleosides show absolute oral bioavailability well above 20%, and there is no affirmative evidence for F<20%; confidence is low because no direct query-specific PK data are available and metabolic deamination could reduce F.
